extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and preclinical HIV/microbicide researchers (PIs, medicinal chemists, virologists, translational scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and experimental/decision criteria for discovery and preclinical evaluation of SEVI-targeting topical microbicide candidates in an R21/R33 NIH project, including biochemical binding assays, cell- and tissue-based efficacy/toxicity assays, and progression milestones for compound advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lipinski’s Rule-of-Five / drug-like properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Obey Lipinski’s Rules of five and are, hence, drug-like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for lead compounds: Mw of BTA-EG4 = 418 g/mol, log P = 1.05, PSA = 91 Å2; BTA-EG6 Mw = 504 g/mol, log P = 1.43, PSA = 73 Å2. Use these drug-like property checks when prioritizing candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding affinity (Kd) to amyloid fibrils / SEVI
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure binding affinity (Kd) of compounds for aggregated amyloid peptides and for SEVI; low micromolar to nanomolar affinities are desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fluorescence binding assays (and FP assays) to determine Kd. Examples: BTA-EG6 Kd = 44 µM for SEVI; oligomeric analogs CC-1/CC-2/CC-3 gave Kd to Aβ of 26/18/2 nM. Expectation: oligomeric derivatives may achieve ≤1 µM affinity for SEVI (≥10-fold improvement vs monomeric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary inhibition efficacy (IC50) against SEVI- and semen-mediated enhancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the IC50 for blockade of SEVI- and semen-mediated enhancement of HIV-1 infection (cell-free assays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary screen in CEM-M7 cells (cell-free HIV-1 + SEVI) is the principal initial assay. Also test cell-free infection with pooled human semen. Use appropriate R5/X4 strains (including transmitted strains) and measure infection (e.g., luciferase, p24). IC50 example: BTA-EG6 IC50 = 13 µM. Use serial dilutions (see dilution guidance) and report IC50s for both SEVI- and semen-mediated enhancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic Index (TI) thresholds for progression
rubrics_metrics.description: Use TI (measure of toxicity vs efficacy) as a gate for advancing compounds through the pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progression to secondary efficacy assays requires TI > 10 for non-colored compounds or TI > 50 for colored compounds. Progression to specialized R33 assays requires TI > 100 (non-colored) or TI > 500 (colored) AND sub-micromolar activity against semen-mediated enhancement in CEM-M7 cells and PBMC. Colored compounds are held to stricter standards due to assay interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay dilution and replication standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize dilution series and replication for efficacy and toxicity assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For assays #1 and #2 (primary efficacy), and for secondary assays, test at least 6 half log10 compound dilutions in triplicate. For IC50 determinations, use serial 2-fold dilutions spanning the active concentration (and fit curves to calculate IC50). Use triplicates and report mean ± SD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary efficacy assay requirements (PBMC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary efficacy assays use primary cells and broader viral panels to confirm activity observed in primary screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress compounds (meeting TI thresholds) to PBMC assays using cells from at least 2 donors. Include testing against (A) 2 transmitted HIV-1 molecular clones, (B) 2 R5-using clade A and C viruses, and (C) a multi-drug resistant virus. Maintain at least 6 half log10 dilutions in triplicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary toxicity assays and TC50 determination in HCEC
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess compound cytotoxicity in cervicovaginal epithelial cells and calculate TC50 to support TI calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary toxicity assays: (1) resazurin (alamarBlue®) in A2En and SiHa cells; (2) Cytotox-Glo (Promega) in A2En and SiHa cells. Test at least 6 half log10 compound dilutions in triplicate and calculate TC50. Use Nonoxynol-9 (0.1% final) as a positive toxicity control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-inflammatory effect on female reproductive tract cells (chemokine release)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether compounds inhibit SEVI-mediated enhancement of virally-induced chemokine release (pro-inflammatory signaling) from HCEC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure chemokines such as IL-8 and CCL20/MIP-3α in A2En and SiHa cell supernatants after exposure to HIV-1 + SEVI ± compound. Reduction of SEVI-enhanced chemokine release is a desired activity that may reduce recruitment of CD4+ target cells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control (QC) of SEVI fibrils
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize SEVI peptide/fibril preparation and QC before use in assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchase single large batch of HPLC-purified PAP[248-286], fibrillize per protocol; confirm fibril formation by ThioT staining and by a physical method (TEM or AFM). Test all peptides/fibrils for LPS using the Limulus amebocyte lysate (LAL) assay and discard if positive. Generate SEVI from disaggregated peptide stocks to remove preformed aggregates/seeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluorescence polarization (FP) binding assay protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an FP displacement assay to evaluate SEVI binding by test compounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preincubate SEVI fibrils with FITC-heparin (a known SEVI binder), add test compound, incubate, and measure polarized fluorescence (mP units). Decreased mP units indicate displacement of FITC-heparin due to compound binding. FP assays have been validated for BTA-EG6 and can be adapted to high-throughput formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening algorithm adapted for SEVI-targeting microbicides
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a screening cascade distinct from conventional antiviral microbicide screens because SEVI-targeting agents do not act directly on the virus and SEVI lacks activity in cell-associated transmission assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal initial screen: cell-free infection with SEVI (CEM-M7). Second tier: cell-free infection with pooled human semen. Triage decisions incorporate activity in the presence of semen and TI thresholds before moving to PBMC and specialized assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colored-compound differential standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply stricter advancement criteria for colored compounds due to assay/color interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use higher TI cutoffs for colored compounds (TI >50 to enter secondary assays; TI >500 to progress to R33 specialized assays). A differential standard for advancement on the basis of color is used as previously explained (ref. 29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicochemical stability testing in relevant fluids
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess compound stability in biologically relevant fluids/materials that mimic the vaginal/semen environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test stability by HPLC and/or MS in (i) seminal plasma, (ii) simulated vaginal fluid at pH 4, and (iii) HEC (universal placebo gel). Incubate compounds for 0–24 hr at 37°C, sampling every 2–4 hr to assess degradation/stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: pH transition assay to mimic semen/vaginal mixing
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate compound performance during the transient pH change that occurs when semen mixes with vaginal fluid during intercourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt the Lackman-Smith et al. method: briefly incubate compounds with target cells at pH 4, mix cell-free R5 virus in 50% semen and dilute into target medium to achieve neutral pH, incubate 1 hr, wash extensively, and perform trans-infection assays. Note: short low-pH exposure has minimal effect on cell viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression cap and ranking for specialized assays
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit number of compounds advanced to specialized, resource-intensive R33 assays and rank by potency/safety metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress no more than 3–4 compounds per year to specialized assays based on relative ranking of TI values and IC50s from primary cell-based assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound synthesis and chemical characterization standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Final test compounds must be well-characterized and of high purity before biological testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All final compounds characterized by NMR and MS, determined to be >95% pure. Report isolated yields for syntheses and document sources of starting materials/reagents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solubility and cytotoxicity benchmarks for candidate molecules
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical and cell-compatibility benchmarks used to triage candidates prior to extensive biological testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer molecules with aqueous solubility >1 mg/mL and no significant toxicity to SH-SY5Y cells at up to 100 µM. These properties, along with drug-like metrics, inform candidate selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of controls, replicates and statistical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard data reporting practices for reproducibility and statistical inference in all assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report mean values from triplicate measurements with standard deviation. Use appropriate statistical tests (examples shown: one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post-test) and indicate significance levels (e.g., * p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001). Include number of independent experiments when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC50 calculation method and curve fitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Define method to derive IC50 values from dose–response data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use serial dilutions spanning the active concentration, collect triplicate measurements, and fit an exponential decay (or appropriate dose–response) curve to calculate the IC50. Example: fit curve to data from CEM-M7 infections as done for BTA-EG6 to determine IC50.
